title: Three Core Pricing Strategies Explained
description: Learn the fundamentals of cost-plus, value-based, and competitive pricing and when to use each approach.

interactions.prompt: A bakery spends $2 on ingredients and labor per cupcake and adds a 50% markup. What pricing method is this?

options.text: Cost-plus pricing
Value-based pricing
Competitive pricing
Dynamic pricing

interactions.teachingPreamble: Cost-plus pricing is the simplest method: calculate your total cost, then add a fixed percentage markup to determine the price. For example, a furniture manufacturer that spends $200 to build a table and applies a 40% markup would price it at $280.

interactions.prompt: A SaaS tool costs $5/month to host per user. Company A charges $15/user, Company B charges $50/user. Company B's customers report 3x higher productivity gains. What explains the price gap?

options.text: Company B has higher hosting costs
Company B uses value-based pricing tied to customer outcomes
Company A is using value-based pricing
Company B is overcharging and will lose customers

chartData.title: SaaS Pricing vs Cost Structure Comparison

interactions.prompt: Salesforce prices its CRM based on how much revenue it helps customers generate, not its development cost. What strategy is this?

options.text: Cost-plus pricing with high margins
Competitive pricing to match rivals
Value-based pricing anchored to customer benefit
Penetration pricing to gain market share

interactions.teachingPreamble: Value-based pricing sets prices according to how much value the customer perceives or receives, not what it costs to produce. Pharmaceutical companies often use this approach  -  a cancer drug that extends life by years can be priced far above its manufacturing cost because the value to patients is enormous.

interactions.prompt: When Burger King sets its Whopper price by looking at what McDonald's charges for a Big Mac, this is called ____ pricing.

options.text: Cost-plus
Competitive
Value-based
Premium

interactions.prompt: You're launching a new project management tool. Asana charges $11/user/month and Monday.com charges $9/user/month. Your cost is $3/user. Do you price at $8 to undercut competitors, or $14 because your AI features save teams 5 hours/week?

options.text: Price at $8  -  win customers fast with a lower price
Price at $14  -  capture value from unique AI time savings
Price at $3.50  -  just cover costs and grow volume
Price at $10  -  split the difference between competitors

interactions.prompt: Netflix raised prices by $2/month and lost only 0.1% of subscribers. What does this tell you about their customers' price sensitivity?

options.text: Customers are highly price sensitive
Customers have low price sensitivity (inelastic demand)
Netflix underpriced by exactly $2
Customers didn't notice the price change

interactions.teachingPreamble: Price sensitivity measures how much customer demand changes when you raise or lower prices. When customers see few alternatives or deeply value your product, they're less price sensitive  -  economists call this inelastic demand. Luxury brands like Rolex thrive on low price sensitivity, while commodity products like generic paper towels face very high price sensitivity.

interactions.prompt: Rank these products from MOST price sensitive (customers will switch over small price changes) to LEAST price sensitive: (a) Generic bottled water, (b) Insulin medication, (c) Starbucks coffee, (d) Gasoline at a highway rest stop with no other stations.

options.text: Generic bottled water
Insulin medication
Starbucks coffee
Gasoline at an isolated highway rest stop

interactions.prompt: You've been using cost-plus pricing at a 40% markup on your handmade candles ($7 cost, $9.80 price). A viral TikTok review calls your candles 'the best stress-relief product under $20' and demand triples overnight. What should you do?

options.text: Keep $9.80  -  your costs haven't changed
Raise to $16.99  -  shift to value-based pricing on perceived benefit
Lower price to $7.50 to maximize the viral moment
Raise to $25  -  charge as much as possible while trending

interactions.priorContext: Previously you were using cost-plus pricing for a simple handmade candle business. Now a viral social media moment has dramatically increased perceived value and demand, forcing you to reconsider your pricing strategy.
